partner_result.actual_application: After aggregating a rank-one zero-curvature star bank L into W=sqrt(2)L, pivot the one curved leaf lambda. The exact Schur determinant is -B^2/2, so the partner theorem gives ||p||_inf <= C_* 2^(1/4)/sqrt(|lambda|B).

compatible_peer_result.actual_application: For the null-center diffuse-star family a=b=0, lambda=B=1, after bank aggregation it yields the sharper uniform bound 2^(13/8)sqrt(15)=11.9459136863.

new_claims.statement: For Q=aX^2+2bXY+lambda Y^2+2X sum c_k Z_k with independent cap-one inputs, B=||c||_2>0 and lambda!=0, ||p_Q||_inf <=27.8162566596/sqrt(|lambda|B). If the resulting rank-three star matrix has all three nonzero eigenvalues of modulus at least one, then B>=1 and |lambda|>=1, so ||p_Q||_inf<27.817.

For c_k=m^(-1/2), a=b=0, lambda=1, the target spectrum is {-1,1,1}; every one-bank-atom local null-pair payment grows like m^(3/8), while aggregate-first payment is uniformly bounded, and the null-pair peer theorem gives <=11.9459136863 after aggregation.
